olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: On a circle, six points $A,B,C,D,E,F$ are chosen randomly, independently, and uniformly. Find the probability that triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are disjoint (share no common points).
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1983

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Prove the roots of $x^5+ax^4+bx^3+cx^2+dx+e=0$ cannot all be real if $2a^2<5b$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1983

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Each set of a finite family of subsets of a line is a union of two closed intervals, and any three sets have a common point. Prove some point belongs to at least half the sets.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1983

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Six segments $S_1,\ldots,S_6$ are congruent to edges $AB,AC,AD,BC,BD,CD$ of tetrahedron $ABCD$. Construct a segment congruent to the altitude from $A$ using straight-edge and compass.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1983

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: An open interval of length $1/n$ on the real line contains at most $\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor$ irreducible fractions $p/q$ with $1\leq q\leq n$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1983
